title_en: The annunciation to Maryam and the birth of Isa
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The angels said: O Maryam, God has chosen you, purified you and chosen you over the women of the worlds.

The angels said that God gives her glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, held in honour in this world and the next and among those brought near; he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and will be among the righteous.
Maryam withdrew from her family to a place in the east and took a screen apart from them.
God sent Our spirit to her; she said: I seek refuge in the Merciful from you, if you fear God.
He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy.

She said: how can I have a boy when no human has touched me and I am not unchaste; he said that this is what her Lord said, that it is easy for Him, that He would make him a sign for people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed.
God says that He creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be", and it is.

chapters.summary_md: The angels told Maryam that God had chosen her and gave her glad tidings of a word from Him, the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam [c1][c2]. She asked how she could have a boy when no human had touched her, and the answer was that her Lord said it is easy for Him [c6].
chapters.body_md:
The angels said: O Maryam, God has chosen you, purified you and chosen you over the women of the worlds [c1]. They said that God gives her glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, held in honour in this world and the next and among those brought near [c2]. He will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and will be among the righteous [c2].

Maryam withdrew from her family to a place in the east and took a screen apart from them [c3]. God sent Our spirit to her; she said: I seek refuge in the Merciful from you, if you fear God [c4]. He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy [c5].

She said: how can I have a boy when no human has touched me and I am not unchaste [c6]. He said that this is what her Lord said, that it is easy for Him, that He would make him a sign for people and a mercy from Him, and that it was a matter decreed [c6]. God says that He creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be", and it is [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The passages give the same answer in different words: in one it is easy for God, and in the other God creates what He wills [c6][c7]. The ayat name him the Messiah and Isa son of Maryam, and say his place is held in honour in this world and the next [c2]. The form in which the spirit came to her is not described in this draft [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The angels told Maryam that God had chosen her [c1]. They gave her glad tidings of a son called Isa, who would speak to people even in the cradle [c2]. Maryam asked how it could be, and the answer was that it is easy for God [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set the question of how beside the statement that God creates what He wills [c6][c7]. Another is that Maryam's first words to the spirit are words of refuge in the Merciful [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when or where the glad tidings came, or how old Maryam was; the ayat say only that she withdrew to a place in the east.
- Not established: the form in which the spirit came to her; the ayah speaks of it and this draft does not describe it.
- Not established: how the glad tidings of 3:45 and the message of 19:19 relate in order; the passages are read as one event.
- Not established: how the pregnancy began beyond what the ayat state.

claims.statement_en: She conceived him and withdrew with him to a place far away.
The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree; she said she wished she had died before this and been forgotten.
She was called from beneath her: do not grieve, your Lord has placed a stream beneath you; shake the trunk of the palm toward you and fresh ripe dates will fall; eat, drink and be content.
She was told that if she saw any human, she should say that she had vowed a fast to the Merciful and would not speak to any person that day.
She pointed to him; they asked how they could speak to one in the cradle, a child; he said: I am a servant of God, He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.
He said that peace was on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive; this is Isa son of Maryam, a word of truth about which they doubt.
God made Maryam, who guarded her chastity, and her son a sign for the worlds; He breathed into her of Our spirit and sheltered them on elevated ground with a place for settlement and flowing water.
Maryam, daughter of Imran, confirmed the words of her Lord and His books and was among the devout.

chapters.summary_md: Maryam conceived and withdrew to a place far away, and the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree [c1][c2]. The child spoke from the cradle, saying he was a servant of God, and God made Maryam and her son a sign for the worlds [c5][c7].
chapters.body_md:
She conceived him and withdrew with him to a place far away [c1]. The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm tree; she said she wished she had died before this and been forgotten [c2].

She was called from beneath her: do not grieve, your Lord has placed a stream beneath you; shake the trunk of the palm toward you and fresh ripe dates will fall; eat, drink and be content [c3]. She was told that if she saw any human, she should say that she had vowed a fast to the Merciful and would not speak to any person that day [c4].

She pointed to him; they asked how they could speak to one in the cradle, a child; he said: I am a servant of God, He has given me the Book and made me a prophet [c5]. He said that peace was on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive; this is Isa son of Maryam, a word of truth about which they doubt [c6].

God made Maryam, who guarded her chastity, and her son a sign for the worlds; He breathed into her of Our spirit and sheltered them on elevated ground with a place for settlement and flowing water [c7]. Maryam, daughter of Imran, confirmed the words of her Lord and His books and was among the devout [c8].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat on the cradle speech are partly reported by the child and partly closed by the ayah calling him Isa son of Maryam and a word of truth [c5][c6]. The other passages describe Maryam and her son as a sign and speak of her as one who guarded her chastity, confirmed God's words and was among the devout [c7][c8]. The ayat do not say who called her from beneath her [c3].
chapters.kids_md: When Isa was born, Maryam was told to eat and drink and not to be sad [c3]. She pointed to the baby, and he spoke from the cradle and said he was a servant of God [c5]. God made Maryam and her son a sign for all the worlds [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the account sets her distress beside the words do not grieve [c2][c3]. Another is that the passages call Maryam devout and her son a sign for the worlds [c7][c8].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the place far away was, how long Maryam stayed there, or who was with her.
- Not established: who called to her from beneath her; the Arabic can be read as a person or as the one under her.
- Not established: how the people reacted beyond the words the ayat record, or how long after the birth they came.
- Not established: the date or the day of the birth.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the birth of Isa and on Maryam. None is used in this draft.
The event is told at greater length in the draft for Isa (content/stories); this event draft stays inside its own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state.

The caller in 19:24 (who called from beneath her) is read in more than one way in commentary; a scholar should decide whether the page names a reading. The words to be spoken to the people (19:26) are reported speech and nothing more.
The chapters omit 3:43-44, 19:27-28 and 19:31-32; 19:27-28 refers by name to another figure, which this draft does not repeat.
